title: I'm training a custom LoRA to generate pixel art for our game. Any advice?
author: GrayMansion_Dev
selftext:
![img](a5ey0h9zlwzh1 "One of the best sprites I got so far")

So, we're a small team of 3 people with no artist and we were struggling to produce enough art for the game, so I decided to experiment with training a custom LoRA to help with asset production.

Well, first of all, I'm looking for some advices, because I've been in this for about 3 weeks and I think there are a lot of things I could've messed up with. I'm still looking for improvements and I know there are some.

I use [ComfyUI](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI) as interface. I also use [SDXL](https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0) and [Pixel Art LoRA](https://huggingface.co/nerijs/pixel-art-xl) not to train my model from scratch and [ControlNet](https://huggingface.co/xinsir/controlnet-scribble-sdxl-1.0) — it really helps with object composition and geometry

![img](ucw92me7pwzh1 "SDXL -> Pixel Art LoRA -> My Custom LoRA")

![img](xnk3sy8yowzh1 "ControlNet nodes")

I have a dataset consists of isolated sprites on plain backgrounds, each paired with a text caption describing the object, shape, size, materials, and viewing angle. ChatGPT helped a lot with preparing it. I also use hand-prepared Scribble ControlNet images to constrain the generated geometry. I use sd-scripts for training and the best I've got so far is a LoRA trained for 25 epochs and I recently generated over 600 sprites, which were actually quite decent.

https://i.redd.it/antape2npwzh1.png

So I've made some progress, but I'm still struggling with consistency and quality. I'd especially appreciate advice on improving the dataset, LoRA training, and ControlNet workflow.

https://i.redd.it/spkpvkzvpwzh1.png

![img](crq38kzvpwzh1 "Some of the recent graphics")

comments.author: Tonmy_
comments.body:
Ok, so, I spent quite a few time training pixel Loras in different game specific art styles (all pixel art), and I’m not understating how long and how many approaches I tried. 

Just fast forwarding my favorite method is actually having codex and his image gen, using reference images and concept arts then generating the assets and human reviewing them. 

The thing with games is that you need the consistency and coherence, not just beautiful random images. I’ve seen people liking pixel lab, a paid service, that is a shortcut too.

The biggest tip that I could give you is that the quality and consistency is highly depend on the model size, so try searching for other models. I think older flux like 2 has a Klein that has permissive license, the others you need to license. There might be some new qwen you could try.

The pitfall here is that the model should have a high number of layers. So there is a flux turbo for example that has too few number of layers, basically using lora in it is a fail.

But of course, this means that you need a more powerful gpu to train, and also do some gimmicks like doing all the text encoding and caching, to train the image generation model.

Each model has its best recipe to training Lora’s, you probably should get ChatGPT or Claude to find them for you and write them down.

Bigger models land you coherent sprites. Then with a bit of tricks you can get an agent to fix the pallet automatically and consistently by code.

IMO unless you have access to bigger models and can train them, you are better off using either pixel lab or codex image gen. As I said earlier, my “this is good and usable enough” is to create concept arts and then from those you generate the sprites.

For example, I have a concept art that has spike hazards, then we generate another concept art using the first  as reference but with spike hazards on it, only then to generate the sprites. (You also can generate several sprites variations on the same image to be efficient )

replies.author: GrayMansion_Dev
replies.body: Thanks for info. I'll try some other models and options to train. I tried pixel lab not very long time ago and it actually does its job and creates usable graphics when I spend some time building correct prompt and collecting references but I just want to try create my own and train it for our game style

replies.author: Tonmy_
replies.body:
Go for bigger models then.

You might experiment with flux dev to see if they do a better job to achieve your vision, though you can’t use them commercially without a license.
